curation.lead:
Erebor Bank, N.A. (FDIC CERT 59378, OCC Charter 25357) is a federally chartered national bank incorporated in Columbus, Ohio, co-founded by Palmer Luckey and Joe Lonsdale with backing from Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, 8VC, Lux Capital, and Andreessen Horowitz. The bank raised $350 million at a $4.35 billion valuation and launched with approximately $635 million in total committed capital [Finding #4684, Finding #4753]. The OCC granted preliminary conditional approval on October 15, 2025 under control number 2025-Charter-342076 (Charter 25357), the FDIC approved deposit insurance on December 16, 2025, and the bank opened for business on February 6, 2026 [Finding #11180, Finding #4945].

The OCC approval letter was signed to Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP partner Wendy M. Goldberg as counsel of record, and explicitly cites Brooks-era OCC Interpretive Letters #1170 (July 20, 2020) and #1174 (January 4, 2021) together with the Hood/Gould-era IL #1184 (May 7, 2025) as the legal scaffold authorizing the bank to hold non-asset-backed virtual currencies on balance sheet under 12 USC 24(Seventh) [Finding #11180]. Application counsel of record was Adam J. Cohen, who filed the charter application on June 11, 2025, then was named OCC Senior Deputy Comptroller and Chief Counsel effective August 11, 2025 — placing him in supervisory authority over bank licensing 65 days before Erebor's conditional approval [Finding #11184].

The board of directors named in the OCC approval letter includes Palmer Luckey (Director and Principal Shareholder; founder of Anduril Industries), Diogo Mónica (Independent Director and co-founder of Anchorage Digital, the holder of the prototypical 2021 OCC crypto-bank charter), Michael Mosier (Independent Director and former Acting Director of FinCEN), and Owen Rapaport, Jacob Hirshman, Michael Hagedorn, Trevor Capozza, Richard Grant, Vlad Dubinsky, and Aaron Pelz [Finding #11181]. Senator Elizabeth Warren's February 25, 2026 letter to Comptroller Jonathan Gould stated that the OCC's process 'may have been contaminated by backroom political manipulation' [Finding #11184]. Warren's March 25, 2025 pre-confirmation letter to Gould had previously demanded a four-year cooling-off period from representing national banks following his service as Comptroller and asked whether he would approve a merger directed by the White House after a payment to the President or his family [Finding #11198].

sections.title: Charter Approval and Conditions
sections.content:
Erebor filed its OCC national bank charter application on June 11, 2025 [Finding #11184]. OCC Comptroller Jonathan Gould granted preliminary conditional approval on October 15, 2025 under OCC Control Number 2025-Charter-342076, Charter 25357, with companion residency waivers under 12 USC 72 (control number 2025-Waiver-342510) for six of the eleven organizers and directors [Finding #11180, Finding #11181]. The FDIC Board approved deposit insurance on December 16, 2025, and the full charter became effective February 6, 2026 [Finding #4945, Finding #7029].

Wendy M. Goldberg of Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP appears as counsel of record on the approval letter. The organizing entity Erebor Group Inc., a Delaware corporation, merges into the bank under 12 USC 215a-3, and existing subsidiary Atticus Digital Inc. becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary post-merger [Finding #11180]. The OCC imposed a 12 percent Tier 1 leverage ratio condition for the first three years — well above the standard 9 percent Community Bank Leverage Ratio — together with deposit-failure-processing protocols, Capital Call Agreement enforcement rights, and mandatory pre-opening examination [Finding #11180, Finding #4945].

For authority to hold non-asset-backed virtual currencies on balance sheet under 12 USC 24(Seventh), the OCC approval letter relies on three OCC interpretive letters: IL #1170 (July 20, 2020), IL #1174 (January 4, 2021 — the last business day of the Brooks tenure), and IL #1184 (May 7, 2025) [Finding #11180]. The first two letters were authored under Acting Comptroller Brian Brooks; IL #1184 was issued in the current administration. Records indicate that the framework Brooks wrote at the OCC, and later served alongside at Bitfury, supplies the operative scaffolding for the Erebor charter [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Board, Management, and Principal Shareholders
sections.content:
The OCC approval letter names eleven organizers, directors, and senior officers [Finding #11181]. Owen Rapaport (CEO, Director, and Principal Shareholder) is the former CEO of Aer Compliance, the regulatory technology firm acquired by StarCompliance, with prior tenures at Bain & Company and the Electrum bitcoin wallet [Finding #7021, Finding #11181]. Jacob E. Hirshman (Chief Strategy Officer, Director, and Principal Shareholder) was previously a regulatory adviser to Circle Internet Financial, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, and an associate at Sullivan & Cromwell [Finding #7021]. Michael Hagedorn (President and Director) is a former Senior Vice President at Valley National Bank and a 17-year veteran of Wells Fargo [Finding #7021]. Richard E. Grant (Chief Financial Officer) previously held senior roles at Customers Bank, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan investment banking [Finding #7021]. Trevor Capozza (Independent Director) heads operations at Palmer Luckey's family office [Finding #7021, Finding #11181].

Three directors warrant particular attention. Palmer Luckey sits on the board as a Principal Shareholder; he separately founded Anduril Industries, whose Arsenal-1 manufacturing facility is being built south of Columbus according to Ohio Tech News reporting [Finding #11181, Finding #7030]. Diogo Mónica is an Independent Director and a co-founder of Anchorage Digital, which holds the OCC's prototypical 2021 crypto-bank charter — itself a product of the same Brooks-era interpretive-letter framework now cited in Erebor's approval [Finding #11181]. Michael Mosier is an Independent Director and the former Acting Director of FinCEN [Finding #11181]. The OCC granted residency waivers under 12 USC 72 for Capozza, Hagedorn, Hirshman, Luckey, Mosier, and Rapaport [Finding #11180, Finding #11181].

Joshua Rosenberg, named in the OCC approval letter as Chief Risk Officer with a 22-year career at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, departed before the bank opened for business per Senator Warren's February 25, 2026 letter [Finding #11181, Finding #7021]. Vlad Dubinsky (Chief Credit Officer) and Aaron Pelz (CTO) round out the management team [Finding #11181]. The principal shareholders identified in the approval letter — Luckey, Rapaport, and Hirshman — are joined, according to the investor record, by external backers including Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, Joe Lonsdale's 8VC, Lux Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, and Haun Ventures [Finding #7033, Finding #7273].

sections.title: Brooks-Era Interpretive Letters as Live Legal Scaffold
sections.content:
The OCC approval letter's legal foundation is unusual. To authorize the bank to hold non-asset-backed virtual currencies on balance sheet to pay 'gas fees' under 12 USC 24(Seventh), the letter cites three OCC interpretive letters as authority [Finding #11180]. Two were issued during the 2020-2021 tenure of Acting Comptroller Brian Brooks: IL #1170 on July 20, 2020 (national-bank custody of cryptocurrency assets) and IL #1174 on January 4, 2021 (national-bank participation in independent node verification networks and stablecoin settlement). The third, IL #1184, was issued under the current administration on May 7, 2025 [Finding #11180].

The documentary record indicates that the Brooks-era framework persisted across administration changes as live legal authority and was subsequently cited by counsel from the same chartering channel [Finding #11236]. The same records reveal a three-link revolving door — Adam Cohen (Skadden to OCC), Diogo Mónica (Anchorage Digital, the prototype crypto-bank charter), and Jonathan Gould (Bitfury Group to OCC) — operating around the same Brooks-era interpretive-letter framework cited in both the Anchorage charter in 2021 and the Erebor charter in 2025 [Finding #11204].

Jonathan Gould's prior employment, as listed in Senator Warren's March 25, 2025 pre-confirmation letter, identifies Bitfury alongside BlackRock and Promontory Financial Group as senior roles preceding his OCC appointment [Finding #11198]. Corporate registry records show Brian Brooks himself on the Bitfury Group Ltd UK 11441275 board following his OCC tenure, putting two consecutive ex-Bitfury executives in the Comptroller's office across two administrations [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Adam J. Cohen: Skadden Application to OCC Approval
sections.content:
Adam J. Cohen joined Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP in May 2024 as co-head of the Financial Institutions Regulatory Group [Finding #11184]. On June 11, 2025 he filed Erebor's OCC national bank charter application on behalf of the organizers [Finding #11184]. OCC press release NR-OCC-2025-76, dated July 30, 2025, announced Cohen's appointment as Senior Deputy Comptroller and Chief Counsel effective August 11, 2025 — sixty-one days after he filed Erebor's application [Finding #11184].

The OCC granted preliminary conditional approval on October 15, 2025; Cohen had then served as OCC Chief Counsel for sixty-five days [Finding #11184]. The approval letter was addressed to Wendy M. Goldberg of Cohen's former Skadden practice [Finding #11180, Finding #11184]. Warren's letter posed Questions 8 through 10 demanding documentation of Cohen's recusals and asking whether Gould had 'discussed Erebor's application with Mr. Cohen either before or after he joined the OCC' and whether Gould 'was aware he served as counsel to Erebor and submitted the company's charter application' when Cohen was hired [Finding #11184]. Cohen's prior government experience, according to the OCC biography and contemporaneous reporting, includes the Federal Reserve Board of Governors and the CFTC, and he previously served as general counsel at SoFi [Finding #11184, Finding #7023].

Examination of the documented timeline shows a 65-day window between Cohen's assumption of OCC supervisory authority over bank licensing and the conditional approval of his most recent client's charter application [Finding #11236]. In parallel, LDA records show that Erebor Group Inc. retained Rich Feuer Anderson for banking and financial-institutions lobbying with effective date June 1, 2025 — the same month as the charter application — through lobbyists with prior service at the Treasury Department, Senate Banking Committee, House Financial Services Committee, and the House Majority Leader's office [Finding #7019, Finding #7261].

sections.title: The Warren Probe and the Recusal Question
sections.content:
On February 25, 2026, Senator Elizabeth Warren, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, sent letters to OCC Comptroller Jonathan Gould, FDIC Chair Travis Hill, and Palmer Luckey regarding the Erebor charter approval, writing that the OCC's process 'may have been contaminated by backroom political manipulation' [Finding #7028, Finding #11184]. The letter cited a fundraising memo, according to Business Insider, describing a co-founder's 'unique connectivity to banking regulators' — including Comptroller Gould — and predicting approval by end of 2025; conditional approval came within four months of application [Finding #7028, Finding #11204].

Warren's March 25, 2025 pre-confirmation letter to Comptroller-designate Gould posed more than one hundred questions across regulation, supervision, bank-merger review, crypto assets, ethics, and agency independence [Finding #11198]. Question 2 demanded a four-year recusal commitment for matters related to former clients; Question 6 requested a four-year cooling-off period from representing national banks after the Comptroller's service; Question 5 asked whether Gould would approve a merger directed by the White House after a payment to the President or his family [Finding #11198]. The same letter listed Bitfury alongside BlackRock, Promontory Financial Group, and the Senate Banking Committee as Gould's prior senior roles [Finding #11198].

Records show that Erebor was the first material chartering action under Gould — an application reviewed by Cohen as Chief Counsel after the same application had been submitted by Cohen as a Skadden partner [Finding #11198, Finding #11204]. Examination of that sequence raises a recusal-voidability question — under federal ethics regulations and OCC internal procedures, if Cohen's involvement after his appointment was not properly walled off, aspects of the approval may be voidable [Finding #11204]. The OCC had not publicly released recusal documentation as of this writing.

sections.title: Structural Significance: Durable Deregulation Scaffolding
sections.content:
Analysis of the documentary record indicates that Erebor is a case in which deregulatory artifacts outlive the administration that produced them [Finding #11236]. The mechanism has four moving parts. First, OCC Interpretive Letters #1170 and #1174 were authored under Acting Comptroller Brian Brooks in July 2020 and January 2021 respectively. Second, the letters survived the entire Biden administration as live legal authority without being rescinded. Third, the framework was supplemented in May 2025 by IL #1184 issued under the Hood and Gould tenures. Fourth, the records show the entire stack cited as authority in the Erebor approval letter signed October 15, 2025 to a partner at the same firm that filed the application [Finding #11180, Finding #11236].

On this record, two institutional channels converge on the Erebor approval [Finding #11236, Finding #11204]. Corporate-registry and Senate Banking Committee records show the first as a Bitfury-to-OCC channel: Brian Brooks served on the Bitfury Group Ltd UK 11441275 board following his 2020-2021 OCC tenure, and Jonathan Gould served as Bitfury Chief Legal Officer from 2022 to 2025 before his confirmation as the 32nd Comptroller [Finding #11198, Finding #11236]. The second is a Skadden-to-OCC channel: Adam J. Cohen joined Skadden in May 2024, filed the Erebor application in June 2025, and was named OCC Chief Counsel in August 2025 [Finding #11184]. Analysis of the approval letter shows the two channels meeting in one document, which Comptroller Gould's office signed and which OCC Chief Counsel Cohen's law department oversaw — addressed to a partner at Cohen's former firm [Finding #11180, Finding #11204].

Read together, the records reveal a single structure: the Brooks-era deregulation framework, written when Brooks ran the OCC and then carried into the private sector when Brooks served at Bitfury, is the legal scaffold under which a Bitfury-affiliated Comptroller chartered a bank advised by his Chief Counsel's old law firm — for backers who include Palmer Luckey, Peter Thiel, and Joe Lonsdale [Finding #11204, Finding #11236]. According to the same synthesis, the Brooks-era framework is cited in connection with the World Liberty Financial token and the stablecoin flows associated with Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Founding, Capital, and Geography
sections.content:
Palmer Luckey conceived Erebor Bank following the March 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, identifying a gap in banking services for venture-backed technology and defense companies [Finding #4753]. He co-founded the bank with Joe Lonsdale, who also co-founded a data-analytics firm with Peter Thiel in 2003 and later founded 8VC [Finding #4684, Finding #11181]. According to investor-disclosure reporting, Lux Capital led the $350 million fundraising round at a $4.35 billion pre-money valuation; co-investors include Founders Fund, 8VC, Andreessen Horowitz, and Haun Ventures, with total committed capital of approximately $635 million [Finding #4753, Finding #7033].

Erebor is registered at 500 Neil Avenue, Suite 140, Columbus, OH 43215 (Franklin County; FDIC CERT 59378; OCC Charter 25357; Federal Reserve RSSD 6053129; LEI 254900S59ZHI2UFM9J76) and operates a single office with no branches [Finding #4944, Finding #4946, Finding #7014]. According to Ohio Tech News and the broader press record, Columbus is also the location of Anduril Industries' Arsenal-1 autonomous-weapons manufacturing facility — Luckey's flagship production site, supported by a $310 million Ohio grant — despite both Luckey and Lonsdale being based in California and Texas respectively [Finding #7030].
